Here's a regex that matches an ISO 8601 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` is a four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` is a month from 01 to 12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` is a day from 01 to 31.
- `^` and `$` anchor the match to the whole string. To find dates inside longer text, swap them for `\b`:

```regex
\b\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])\b
```

It matches `2026-10-01` and rejects `2026-13-01` and `2026-10-32`.

It doesn't check month lengths or leap years, so `2026-02-31` still matches. Regex alone can't handle that well, so validate those cases with a date parser.
